title: How to write complex software
summary: Describes a top-down layering approach for organizing complex software, where each layer defines the ideal API for the layer below it, emphasizing stub-first implementation and IO-only mocking.
when-to-read: Read this when designing the overall architecture and code organization for a large, complex software project (tens to hundreds of thousands of lines), or when deciding whether to start implementation top-down versus bottom-up. If you're instead looking for specific code quality practices, refactoring patterns, or testing strategies within an already-determined architecture, consult the code-quality or testing tags instead.
